what_it_is_about: One modifier that counts only against a target carrying a tag, and one that counts only from a source carrying one. Four combinations, because a qualification that was read from the wrong side would be right in two of them.
engine_deviation: The reference answers 10.0 for all four variants, and the reason is in Unreal's own source: a persistent aggregator is recomputed with no source or target tags at all - GameplayEffect.cpp, where it does it, says "this is not an execution, so there are no 'source' and 'target' tags to fill out in the FAggregatorEvaluateParameters". So a modifier's own requirement is never met under an infinite effect, whatever either side is carrying. Asked as an execution instead, the same reference answers 10, 15, 17 and 22 - target requirement read from the target, source from the source - which is the question this scenario is named for. GAS_Engine answers those four numbers under an infinite effect too, on purpose: a modifier that carries a condition and silently never counts is a feature that does nothing, and F5.2.3 added this so one effect can hit harder against the undead without being authored twice.
